summary: Sync for your Obsidian vault using git: a watcher commits and pushes after you stop typing, pulls with rebase on a timer, never loses either side of a conflict, refuses to push a suspicious mass deletion, and a status command tells you where things stand. Your phone uses a git client against the same repository.

stack.why: history for free; the conflict model is understood

stack.choice: A bash script on a systemd timer or launchd agent, or Node with chokidar
stack.why: the simpler one for your machine

stack.choice: Working Copy on iOS, a git client on Android

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your Obsidian vault folder, backed up once by hand first
prerequisites.why: You are about to automate commits in it. Take a plain copy before Phase 1 so nothing is at risk while you learn.
prerequisites.get: Copy the vault folder to an external drive or a zip.

prerequisites.name: A private git repository (GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg)
prerequisites.why: The remote is the sync point. Private, because these are your notes.
prerequisites.get: Create an empty private repository. For pushing without passwords, add an SSH key: ssh-keygen -t ed25519, then add the public key in the host's SSH keys settings.

prerequisites.name: A second machine or a phone
prerequisites.why: Every phase is tested across two devices; one machine cannot test sync.
prerequisites.get: Another computer, or a phone with a git client.

prerequisites.name: A mobile git client (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 6: the phone reads and writes the same repository.
prerequisites.get: Working Copy on iOS (one-time purchase for push), MGit or GitJournal on Android.

env.name: DEBOUNCE_SECONDS
env.where: Wait this long after the last change before committing.

env.name: PULL_INTERVAL_MINUTES
env.where: How often to pull with rebase.

env.name: MAX_CHANGED_FILES
env.where: Refuse to auto-commit a change touching more files than this.

phases.title: Repository hygiene
phases.goal: A vault that does not produce a diff just from being opened.

steps.do: git init in the vault and write .gitignore
steps.detail: .obsidian/workspace*, .obsidian/cache, .trash/, .DS_Store. Keep the rest of .obsidian if you want settings to travel.
commands: cd $VAULT_PATH && git init && git remote add origin git@github.com:you/notes.git

steps.do: Open and close Obsidian and check git status is clean

check: git status is clean after launching and closing Obsidian without editing
Opening the vault on the second machine produces no diff

phases.title: Manual round trip
phases.goal: Do the loop by hand before automating it.

steps.do: On machine A: edit a note, commit, push
commands: git add -A && git commit -m 'notes' && git push -u origin main

steps.do: On machine B: pull, edit the same note elsewhere, push; then pull on A and watch the merge

check: A note written on A appears on B and back
You have seen one real merge succeed

phases.title: The watcher
phases.goal: Debounced commits, timed pulls, one git operation at a time.

steps.detail: Debounce DEBOUNCE_SECONDS after the last change, git add -A, commit with the changed-file count, push. Pull --rebase on start and every PULL_INTERVAL_MINUTES. Take a lock file so a commit never races a rebase.

steps.do: Install it as a systemd user timer or a launchd agent

check: Editing a note results in a commit and push within a minute
Ten quick edits produce one commit
A network outage is caught up when the network returns
A manual git command while idle is not clobbered

phases.title: Conflicts, without data loss
phases.goal: Both versions survive, the vault is never left mid-rebase, the daemon keeps running.

steps.do: On rebase conflict, keep local, write the incoming version as <name>.conflict-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md, commit, log loudly
Create a conflict deliberately with both machines offline and bring them back

check: The vault is not left mid-rebase
traps: Test this before trusting the sync with anything you care about.

phases.title: Status and safety
phases.goal: Know the state, and never propagate a mass deletion.

steps.do: Write vaultsync status: last push, last pull, pending, conflict files, daemon alive
Add the MAX_CHANGED_FILES guard that asks instead of committing

check: Deleting a folder of 200 notes triggers the guard
status reports an unresolved conflict file

phases.title: Mobile and second machine
phases.goal: Documentation only: a phone and another computer set up from the README.

steps.do: Write the README: second-machine setup, the conflict-file convention, the size-guard override
Set up the phone client against the same repository and write one note from it
steps.detail: Working Copy on iOS, MGit or GitJournal on Android.

check: A second machine is set up from the README alone
A note written on the phone reaches the desktop

phases.title: Operate it
phases.goal: Only for the careful path: know when sync stops, keep an off-git backup, encrypt if the remote should not read your notes.

steps.do: Alert when the last successful push is older than a day
steps.detail: A cron job that checks and posts to ntfy or a webhook.

steps.do: Nightly tarball of the vault to a second place, independent of git
If the remote must be zero-knowledge, use git-crypt or a full-vault age-encrypted archive instead, and accept the mobile cost
steps.detail: Decide this consciously; do not half-build encryption.

check: Stopping the daemon produces an alert the next day
The tarball restores to a readable vault

product.outcome: Sync you understand completely: every change in history, conflicts that never lose a word, and a warning before a mistake spreads.

architecture.swap: The conflict-file convention is the contract

operations.backup: git is history, not backup: a nightly tarball to a second place.
operations.restore: git clone, or extract the tarball.
operations.monitoring: Alert when the last push is stale.
operations.incident: A bad commit is reverted with git; a conflict file is resolved by reading both versions.

releaseGate: Conflict drill performed on two offline machines
Second machine set up from the README

notIncluded: An encrypted-vault workflow by default; it is a different design with mobile costs.
A version-history UI; git log is the history.
Mobile beyond configuring an existing client.
after: A small web viewer of the repository for read-only access anywhere
